questions.prompt: How does the guide's interview summary describe `ALTER`?
options: It drops an object and recreates it with the new definition
It copies a table into a new one with changes applied
It changes the data stored in rows
It modifies existing objects such as tables, constraints, indexes, views and procedures without dropping and recreating them
questions.explanation: `ALTER` changes an object's definition in place. Changing row data is `UPDATE`'s job.

questions.prompt: Grades in `Enrollments` must be one of A, B, C, D or F. Which `ALTER` usage does the guide map to "enforce business rule"?
questions.explanation: The real-world usage table maps "Enforce business rule" to `ADD CHECK`; a CHECK constraint rejects values outside the allowed set.

questions.prompt: You try to shrink `StudentName` with `ALTER COLUMN StudentName NVARCHAR(20)`, but some names are longer than 20 characters. What does the guide warn?
options: The long names are silently cut to 20 characters
You can't shrink the size if data truncation would occur
The rows with long names are deleted
questions.explanation: Changing a column's type or size is allowed only when the existing data still fits; shrinking below existing values would truncate data, so it is refused.

questions.prompt: Why might dropping the primary key `PK_Students` fail?
options: Primary keys can never be dropped once created
A foreign key, such as one in another table, still references it
The table has a DEFAULT constraint
The database is in READ_WRITE mode
questions.explanation: The important notes say you can't drop a PK while an FK references it, and you can't modify a column that is used in an index or constraint.
